message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic, modern, and cult‑favorite horror films you might enjoy:

| # | Title | Year | Why it’s worth watching |
|---|-------|------|--------------------------|
| 1 | **The Shining** | 1980 | A masterful psychological thriller with iconic imagery. |
| 2 | **Hereditary** | 2018 | A chilling family drama that redefines dread. |
| 3 | **Get Out** | 2017 | A smart social satire wrapped in horror. |
| 4 | **A Quiet Place** | 2018 | Tension built on silence and sound design. |
| 5 | **The Conjuring** | 2013 | A modern supernatural franchise grounded in real‑life cases. |
| 6 | **It Follows** | 2014 | A fresh take on the “invisible threat” trope. |
| 7 | **Midsommar** | 2019 | A daylight horror that’s as unsettling as it is beautiful. |
| 8 | **The Babadook** | 2014 | A psychological horror that doubles as a mother‑daughter drama. |
| 9 | **The Witch** | 2015 | A slow‑burn, atmospheric period horror. |
|10 | **Paranormal Activity** | 2007 | Low‑budget found‑footage that still terrifies. |
|11 | **The Ring** | 2002 | A modern retelling of a Japanese horror classic. |
|12 | **Suspiria** (2018) | 2018 | A visually striking remake of the 1977 original. |
|13 | **The Cabin in the Woods** | 2012 | A meta‑commentary on horror tropes. |
|14 | **It** | 2017 | A nostalgic, campy adaptation of Stephen King’s novel. |
|15 | **The Others** | 2001 | A gothic thriller with a twist ending. |

Feel free to pick based on your mood—whether you want psychological dread, supernatural chills, or a bit of horror‑comedy. Enjoy the scares!
